drafter.private_reasoning: Prepare an employer-protective opening draft: make compensation subject to applicable plans, condition severance on a release and compliance, and define a reasonable scope for the restrictive covenant. Remove internal comments and document properties before transmission; do not disclose confidential negotiating limits.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Please find Vireo’s opening draft. We have clarified the compensation and severance mechanics and proposed a defined, appropriately limited post-employment restriction. We welcome your comments and are available to discuss the terms.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive the annual base salary specified in the applicable compensation schedule, payable in accordance with the Company’s ordinary payroll practices and subject to applicable tax withholdings. The Executive may participate in benefit and incentive plans for which the Executive is eligible, in each case subject to the terms of the applicable plan and the Company’s policies as in effect from time to time. No incentive compensation is earned or payable except as provided under the applicable plan.

3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, the Executive shall be eligible to receive the Severance Amount specified in the applicable compensation schedule, subject to the Executive’s execution and non-revocation of a release of claims in favor of the Company and its affiliates, and continued compliance with the Executive’s obligations under this Agreement. Severance shall be paid in accordance with the applicable schedule and applicable law. The Executive shall not be entitled to severance under this Section if the Executive resigns or is terminated for Cause.

4. NON-COMPETE. During employment and for twelve months following termination of employment, the Executive shall not, within any jurisdiction in which the Executive had material responsibility on behalf of the Company during the final twelve months of employment, directly perform services substantially similar to those performed for the Company for a business that competes materially with the business activities for which the Executive had material responsibility. This restriction does not prohibit passive ownership of up to two percent of a publicly traded company. This Section applies only to the extent permitted by applicable law.

We also propose removing the post-employment non-compete and replacing it, if needed, with a narrowly tailored non-solicitation provision, while making earned compensation and severance payable without forfeiture based on alleged post-termination noncompliance.

Provide a schedule structure with figures expressly left for client confirmation, narrow Cause with notice and cure where practicable, replace the non-compete with a limited non-solicit, and remove continued post-termination compliance as a condition to earned compensation or severance. Preserve a release condition for severance.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you. We have revised the draft to replace the post-employment non-compete with a limited non-solicitation provision, define Cause with notice and an opportunity to cure where curable, and clarify that earned compensation and otherwise payable severance are not forfeited based on alleged post-termination noncompliance. We have also set out the requested compensation-schedule categories and payment mechanics for completion. The economic figures remain to be confirmed and mutually agreed; we have not inserted unapproved amounts. Severance remains conditioned on execution and non-revocation of a customary release.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive the annual base salary set forth in Schedule A, payable in accordance with the Company’s ordinary payroll practices and subject to applicable tax withholdings. The Executive may participate in benefit and incentive plans for which the Executive is eligible, subject to the applicable plan terms and Company policies. Schedule A shall state the annual target incentive opportunity and the applicable performance measures and determination mechanics. Incentive compensation shall be earned and paid in accordance with those terms; any earned but unpaid incentive compensation through the termination date shall be paid when otherwise due under the applicable plan or law, and shall not be forfeited based solely on an alleged post-termination breach of this Agreement. Schedule A shall also specify any severance amount and payment timing.
edits.name: Compensation

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause, the Executive shall be eligible to receive the severance amount and payment timing specified in Schedule A, subject to the Executive’s execution and non-revocation of a release of claims in favor of the Company and its affiliates. Severance shall be paid in accordance with Schedule A and applicable law. Severance shall not be subject to forfeiture or withholding based solely on an allegation that the Executive has failed to comply with a post-termination obligation; this sentence does not limit the Company’s right to pursue any remedy otherwise available for an established breach. The Executive shall not be entitled to severance under this Section if the Executive resigns or is terminated for Cause. For purposes of this Agreement, “Cause” means: (a) the Executive’s willful and material breach of this Agreement or material failure to perform material duties, in either case continuing for 30 days after written notice specifying the breach or failure in reasonable detail; (b) fraud, embezzlement, or other intentional dishonesty in connection with the Executive’s duties; (c) conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony involving dishonesty or moral turpitude; or (d) willful misconduct or gross negligence in performing the Executive’s duties that causes material harm to the Company. Where the conduct constituting Cause is reasonably capable of cure, the Company shall provide written notice and a 30-day opportunity to cure before termination for Cause. No cure period is required for conduct that is not reasonably capable of cure.
edits.name: Severance and Cause

edits.text: 4. NON-SOLICITATION. During employment and for 12 months following termination of employment, the Executive shall not, for the purpose of materially competing with the Company’s business activities for which the Executive had material responsibility during the final 12 months of employment, knowingly solicit any customer or actively solicited prospective customer with whom the Executive had material business contact on the Company’s behalf during that period to terminate or materially reduce its business with the Company. During the same period, the Executive shall not knowingly solicit for employment any employee of the Company with whom the Executive worked materially during the final 12 months of employment; general advertisements and hiring not specifically directed at such employees are not solicitation. This Section applies only to the extent permitted by applicable law.
edits.name: Non-solicitation
